intro: You already know the first conditional: If it rains, I'll stay home. Today you go further: more kinds of result (might, can, an instruction), three useful words (unless, as soon as and in case), and how to use them for warnings, deals and promises at work. Warm-up: what will you do if it rains on your way home today?
teachingNotes: Recap, don't re-teach (the learner has done a2-zero-first-conditional and b1-future-forms): first conditional = if + present simple, will/won't + base form; no will in the if-part (common error *'If it will rain, we'll stay home' → 'If it rains, we'll stay home'; Indonesian 'kalau nanti/besok hujan' pushes learners to put the future in the if-part). The same rule after when, as soon as, until, unless and in case. The new skill here is the result part: will/won't (sure), might/may (not sure), can (possible or allowed: 'If you come before 8, you can park in the basement'; common error *'will can', from Indonesian 'akan bisa'), going to, and an imperative (an instruction: 'If you see Rina, tell her the meeting is at 3', no subject and no will).

unless = if … not (Indonesian 'kecuali kalau' / 'kalau … tidak'): 'Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus' = 'If you don't hurry, …'. The verb after unless is positive, because the 'not' is already inside unless. Common error *'Unless you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus' (a double negative). 'if … not' is always correct; unless is shorter and very common in warnings, rules and conditions ('You can't enter unless you have an ID card'). Don't push unless for feelings caused by something not happening ('I'll be sad if you don't come' is better than 'unless you come'), and only test unless vs if where the meaning makes one of them clearly wrong.

as soon as = begitu / segera setelah: the thing is sure to happen and the result comes right after it (like when, but faster). Present simple after it, even for the future: common error *'As soon as I will finish, I'll call you' → 'As soon as I finish, I'll call you'. Accept the present perfect for a finished action (as soon as I've finished), but teach and test the present simple.

in case = jaga-jaga kalau / siapa tahu: the action is done FIRST, now or before, as a precaution, because something MIGHT happen later. 'Take an umbrella in case it rains' = take it now, rain or no rain. 'Take an umbrella if it rains' = take it only when it's raining. Indonesian 'kalau' covers both, so learners use if for precautions. Present simple after in case (not 'in case it will rain'). 'just in case' at the end = untuk jaga-jaga. On signs, 'In case of fire / emergency' (in case of + a noun) is a formal way to say 'if there is a fire': mention it only so learners aren't confused. Some American speakers also use 'in case' to mean 'if' in offers ('In case you need anything, I'm in room 5'): accept it if the learner uses it, but don't teach or test it.

Real use at work (the 'talk-about-likely' objective): consequences (If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel), warnings (Unless you back up your files, you might lose everything), deals and promises (If you finish the report by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday; As soon as I get approval, I'll let you know) and instructions (If the server goes down, call me). will = sure, might = not sure and softer, can = allowed or possible. Use tech and office contexts: apps, bugs, laptops, passwords, clients, KRL, ojek online, prices in rupiah.

Limits: no second or third conditional (If I had…, I would…), no 'provided / as long as', no 'if you will' (polite will in the if-part), no past perfect, passive or reported speech. If the learner asks about 'If I were you', say it's a later lesson (second conditional) and give it as a phrase to remember.

keyPoints.title: if + present, then many kinds of result
keyPoints.explanation: The if-part stays in the present simple (no will). The result can be will/won't (sure), might (not sure), can (possible or allowed, never 'will can'), going to, or an instruction that starts with the verb: If you see Rina, tell her the meeting is at 3.

id.title: if + present, lalu banyak jenis hasil
id.explanation: Bagian if tetap memakai present simple (tanpa will). Hasilnya bisa will/won't (pasti), might (belum pasti), can (bisa atau boleh, jangan 'will can'), going to, atau perintah yang diawali kata kerja: If you see Rina, tell her the meeting is at 3.

keyPoints.title: unless, as soon as, in case
keyPoints.explanation: unless = if … not (kecuali kalau / kalau tidak); the verb after it is positive: Unless you hurry, not 'Unless you don't hurry'. as soon as = begitu (sure to happen, right after). in case = jaga-jaga kalau: you act first, as a precaution. After all three, use the present simple, never will.

keyPoints.title: Consequences, warnings and promises
keyPoints.explanation: At work, the first conditional tells people what will happen: a consequence (If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel), a warning (Unless you back up your files, you might lose everything) or a promise or deal (If you finish by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday). will = sure, might = not sure and softer, can = allowed.

id.title: Akibat, peringatan dan janji
id.explanation: Di kantor, first conditional memberi tahu orang apa yang akan terjadi: akibat (If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel), peringatan (Unless you back up your files, you might lose everything), atau janji dan kesepakatan (If you finish by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday). will = pasti, might = belum pasti dan lebih halus, can = boleh.

material.title: if + present, then many kinds of result

blocks.text:
Quick recap: a first conditional talks about **one possible situation in the future** and its result: *If it rains, we'll stay inside.* The **if-part** stays in the **present simple**, even about tomorrow, and never takes **will**.

New today: the **result** doesn't have to be *will*. Choose the one that fits:
- **will / won't** + verb: you're sure. *If the traffic is bad, I'll take the KRL.*
- **might** + verb: you're **not sure** (*mungkin*). *If the traffic is bad, I might be late.*
- **can** + verb: it's **possible** or **allowed** (*bisa / boleh*). *If you come before 8, you can park in the basement.*
- **going to** + verb: a result you're quite sure about, or a plan. *If the price goes up again, we're going to look for another supplier.*
- **an instruction**: a sentence that starts with the verb, with no *you* and no *will* (teachers call it an **imperative**, *kalimat perintah*). *If you see Rina, tell her the meeting is at 3.*

id.text:
Ingat lagi: first conditional membicarakan **satu situasi yang mungkin terjadi di masa depan** dan hasilnya: *If it rains, we'll stay inside.* **Bagian if** tetap memakai **present simple**, walaupun tentang besok, dan tidak pernah memakai **will**.

Yang baru hari ini: **hasilnya** tidak harus *will*. Pilih yang cocok:
- **will / won't** + kata kerja: kamu yakin. *If the traffic is bad, I'll take the KRL.*
- **might** + kata kerja: kamu **belum yakin** (*mungkin*). *If the traffic is bad, I might be late.*
- **can** + kata kerja: **bisa** atau **boleh**. *If you come before 8, you can park in the basement.*
- **going to** + kata kerja: hasil yang cukup pasti, atau rencana. *If the price goes up again, we're going to look for another supplier.*
- **perintah**: kalimat yang diawali kata kerja, tanpa *you* dan tanpa *will* (guru menyebutnya **imperative**, *kalimat perintah*). *If you see Rina, tell her the meeting is at 3.*

rows.id: Kalau macet, saya mungkin terlambat.

rows.id: Kalau kamu datang sebelum jam 8, kamu bisa parkir di basement.

rows.id: Kalau harganya naik lagi, kita akan cari pemasok lain.

blocks.text:
**Two Indonesian traps:**
- *Kalau **nanti** hujan …* has a future word, but English doesn't: **If it rains**, not 'If it will rain'.
- *akan bisa* is two words, but English uses one: **you can park**, not 'you will can park'. (*will be able to* is also correct, but *can* is shorter.)

In an instruction, there's no *will* anywhere: *If you see Rina, **tell** her …*, not 'you will tell her'.

id.text:
**Dua jebakan bahasa Indonesia:**
- *Kalau **nanti** hujan …* punya kata masa depan, tapi bahasa Inggris tidak: **If it rains**, bukan 'If it will rain'.
- *akan bisa* ada dua kata, tapi bahasa Inggris cukup satu: **you can park**, bukan 'you will can park'. (*will be able to* juga benar, tapi *can* lebih pendek.)

Dalam kalimat perintah, tidak ada *will* sama sekali: *If you see Rina, **tell** her …*, bukan 'you will tell her'.

blocks.prompt: If the delivery ___ late again, we might change suppliers.
blocks.explain: The if-part stays in the present simple, even about the future: **If the delivery is late**. No will there; *might* goes in the result. 'be' alone has no form for *the delivery* (it → **is**).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: If the delivery ___ late again, we might change suppliers.
id.explain: Bagian if tetap present simple, walaupun tentang masa depan: **If the delivery is late**. Tidak ada will di situ; *might* ada di bagian hasil. 'be' saja tidak cocok untuk *the delivery* (it → **is**).

id.title: if + present, lalu banyak jenis hasil

blocks.text:
**unless** means **if … not** (*kecuali kalau* / *kalau … tidak*):
- *If you **don't hurry**, you'll miss the bus.*
- ***Unless** you **hurry**, you'll miss the bus.* (same meaning)

Look at the verb after unless: it's **positive** (*hurry*, not *don't hurry*). Why? The *not* is already inside **unless**. If you add *don't*, you say 'not' twice and the meaning turns around: 'Unless you don't hurry' = 'if you hurry, you'll miss the bus', which makes no sense.

The rest works like **if**: present simple after unless (no will), a comma when unless comes first, no comma when it comes second: *You can't enter the building unless you have an ID card.*

id.text:
**unless** artinya **if … not** (*kecuali kalau* / *kalau … tidak*):
- *If you **don't hurry**, you'll miss the bus.*
- ***Unless** you **hurry**, you'll miss the bus.* (artinya sama)

Perhatikan kata kerja setelah unless: bentuknya **positif** (*hurry*, bukan *don't hurry*). Kenapa? Kata *not* sudah ada di dalam **unless**. Kalau kamu menambah *don't*, kamu bilang 'tidak' dua kali dan artinya jadi terbalik: 'Unless you don't hurry' = 'kalau kamu cepat, kamu akan ketinggalan bus', dan itu tidak masuk akal.

Selebihnya sama seperti **if**: present simple setelah unless (tanpa will), pakai koma kalau unless di depan, tanpa koma kalau di belakang: *You can't enter the building unless you have an ID card.*

rows.en: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
rows.id: Kalau kamu tidak cepat, kamu akan ketinggalan bus.

rows.en: You can't enter the building unless you have an ID card.
rows.id: Kamu tidak bisa masuk gedung kecuali kalau punya kartu identitas.

rows.en: Unless Pak Hasan says no, we'll start the project on Monday.

rows.id: Ojeknya tidak akan menunggu kalau kamu tidak bayar dulu.
rows.note: won't in the result, present after unless

id.note: won't di bagian hasil, present setelah unless

blocks.text:
**Not sure? if … not is always correct.** *unless* is just shorter, and it's very common in warnings, rules and conditions. For a feeling, English prefers if … not: *I'll be sad if you don't come* (not 'unless you come').

**The Indonesian trap:** *kalau kamu tidak cepat* has *tidak*, so learners keep it: 'Unless you don't hurry'. Drop it: **Unless you hurry**.

id.text:
**Ragu? if … not selalu benar.** *unless* hanya lebih pendek, dan sangat umum dalam peringatan, aturan dan syarat. Untuk perasaan, bahasa Inggris lebih suka if … not: *I'll be sad if you don't come* (bukan 'unless you come').

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *kalau kamu tidak cepat* ada kata *tidak*, jadi pelajar ikut memakainya: 'Unless you don't hurry'. Buang saja: **Unless you hurry**.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means 'If you don't have an ID card, you can't enter the building'?
options: Unless you don't have an ID card, you can't enter the building.
Unless you have an ID card, you can't enter the building.
Unless you have an ID card, you can enter the building.
blocks.explain: unless = if … not, so the verb after it is positive: **Unless you have an ID card, you can't enter.** 'Unless you don't have' says *not* twice, and 'you can enter' changes the meaning.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'If you don't have an ID card, you can't enter the building'?
id.explain: unless = if … not, jadi kata kerja setelahnya positif: **Unless you have an ID card, you can't enter.** 'Unless you don't have' berarti bilang *tidak* dua kali, dan 'you can enter' mengubah artinya.

blocks.text:
You met **as soon as** (*begitu / segera setelah*) in the future-forms lesson. It's like **when**: the first thing is **sure to happen**, and the result comes **right after it**. *As soon as I get the numbers, I'll send you the report.*

Compare: **if** = maybe it happens (*If I get the numbers, …*: I'm not sure I'll get them). **as soon as** = it will happen, and I'll act immediately.

The verb rule is the same as after if: **present simple**, never will: *as soon as I **finish***, not 'as soon as I will finish'. Keep the **-s** with he/she/it: *as soon as the payment **arrives***.

id.text:
Kamu sudah bertemu **as soon as** (*begitu / segera setelah*) di pelajaran bentuk masa depan. Mirip **when**: hal pertama **pasti terjadi**, dan hasilnya datang **langsung setelahnya**. *As soon as I get the numbers, I'll send you the report.*

Bandingkan: **if** = mungkin terjadi (*If I get the numbers, …*: saya belum yakin dapat). **as soon as** = pasti terjadi, dan saya langsung bertindak.

Aturan kata kerjanya sama seperti setelah if: **present simple**, jangan will: *as soon as I **finish***, bukan 'as soon as I will finish'. Tetap pakai **-s** untuk he/she/it: *as soon as the payment **arrives***.

rows.id: Begitu angkanya saya dapat, laporannya saya kirim ke kamu.
rows.note: sure to happen, then right away

rows.en: Call me as soon as you land in Makassar.
rows.id: Telepon saya begitu kamu mendarat di Makassar.

rows.en: We'll start the meeting as soon as Bu Ani arrives.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Nanti begitu sudah selesai, saya telepon* has *nanti* and *sudah*, so learners write 'as soon as I will finish' or 'as soon as I already finish'. English says just **as soon as I finish**. (*as soon as I've finished* is also correct.)

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Nanti begitu sudah selesai, saya telepon* ada *nanti* dan *sudah*, jadi pelajar menulis 'as soon as I will finish' atau 'as soon as I already finish'. Bahasa Inggris cukup **as soon as I finish**. (*as soon as I've finished* juga benar.)

blocks.prompt: I'll call you as soon as the doctor ___ me.
blocks.explain: After **as soon as**, use the present simple even for the future: **as soon as the doctor sees me** (the doctor = he/she → -s). 'will see' is the common mistake.

id.explain: Setelah **as soon as**, pakai present simple walaupun untuk masa depan: **as soon as the doctor sees me** (the doctor = he/she → -s). 'will see' adalah kesalahan yang umum.

material.title: in case: just to be safe

blocks.text:
**in case** = *jaga-jaga kalau* / *siapa tahu*. You do something **first** (now, or before), as a **precaution** (*tindakan berjaga-jaga*), because something **might** happen later.

*Take an umbrella **in case** it rains.* You take the umbrella **now**, before you know the weather. If it rains, you're ready; if it doesn't, no problem. You take it either way.

Compare with **if**: *Take an umbrella **if** it rains.* = take it **only when** it's raining (when you leave). No rain, no umbrella.

Ask yourself: **Do I do it before, just to be safe?** → **in case**. **Do I do it only when the thing happens?** → **if**.

After in case, use the **present simple** too: *in case it **rains***, not 'in case it will rain'.

id.text:
**in case** = *jaga-jaga kalau* / *siapa tahu*. Kamu melakukan sesuatu **lebih dulu** (sekarang, atau sebelumnya), sebagai **tindakan berjaga-jaga**, karena sesuatu **mungkin** terjadi nanti.

*Take an umbrella **in case** it rains.* Kamu membawa payung **sekarang**, sebelum tahu cuacanya. Kalau hujan, kamu siap; kalau tidak hujan, tidak masalah. Payungnya tetap kamu bawa.

Bandingkan dengan **if**: *Take an umbrella **if** it rains.* = bawa payung **hanya kalau** sedang hujan (saat kamu berangkat). Tidak hujan, tidak bawa payung.

Tanya dirimu: **Apakah saya melakukannya lebih dulu, untuk jaga-jaga?** → **in case**. **Apakah saya melakukannya hanya kalau hal itu terjadi?** → **if**.

Setelah in case, pakai **present simple** juga: *in case it **rains***, bukan 'in case it will rain'.

rows.id: Bawa payung, jaga-jaga kalau hujan.
rows.note: you take it now, rain or no rain

rows.en: I'll give you my number in case you get lost.

id.note: just in case di akhir = untuk jaga-jaga

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *kalau* covers both, so learners say 'Bring a jacket if it's cold' when they mean a precaution. If you do it **before**, to be ready, say **in case**: *Bring a jacket in case it's cold in the meeting room.*

**On signs:** *In case of fire, use the stairs* (in case **of** + a noun) is a formal notice that means *Jika terjadi kebakaran*, so there it means *if there is*. That's a fixed phrase for notices; with a full sentence (*in case it rains*), in case means *jaga-jaga kalau*.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *kalau* dipakai untuk keduanya, jadi pelajar bilang 'Bring a jacket if it's cold' padahal maksudnya jaga-jaga. Kalau kamu melakukannya **lebih dulu**, supaya siap, pakai **in case**: *Bring a jacket in case it's cold in the meeting room.*

**Di papan pengumuman:** *In case of fire, use the stairs* (in case **of** + kata benda) adalah pengumuman resmi yang artinya *Jika terjadi kebakaran*, jadi di situ artinya *kalau ada*. Itu frasa tetap untuk pengumuman; dengan kalimat lengkap (*in case it rains*), in case artinya *jaga-jaga kalau*.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani always keeps a spare key at her neighbour's house ___ she loses hers.
blocks.explain: She keeps the key there **always**, before anything happens, just to be safe: **in case** she loses hers. 'if' would mean she puts the key there only after losing hers, which is impossible. 'unless' = if … not, which makes no sense here.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani always keeps a spare key at her neighbour's house ___ she loses hers.
id.explain: Dia **selalu** menyimpan kunci di sana, sebelum terjadi apa-apa, untuk jaga-jaga: **in case** she loses hers. 'if' berarti dia menaruh kunci di sana baru setelah kuncinya hilang, dan itu tidak mungkin. 'unless' = if … not, tidak masuk akal di sini.

blocks.text:
At work, the first conditional is everywhere. It tells people **what will happen**:
- a **consequence** (*akibat*): *If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel the contract.*
- a **warning** (*peringatan*): *Unless you back up your files, you might lose everything.*
- a **deal or promise** (*kesepakatan / janji*): *If you finish the report by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday.* / *As soon as I get approval from Pak Hasan, I'll let you know.*
- an **instruction** for a problem: *If the server goes down, call me.*

Pick the result word by how sure you are: **will** = sure, **might** = not sure (and it sounds softer and more polite in a warning), **can** = allowed or possible.

id.text:
Di kantor, first conditional ada di mana-mana. Kalimat ini memberi tahu orang **apa yang akan terjadi**:
- **akibat**: *If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel the contract.*
- **peringatan**: *Unless you back up your files, you might lose everything.*
- **kesepakatan atau janji**: *If you finish the report by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday.* / *As soon as I get approval from Pak Hasan, I'll let you know.*
- **instruksi** untuk masalah: *If the server goes down, call me.*

Pilih kata di bagian hasil sesuai seberapa yakin kamu: **will** = pasti, **might** = belum pasti (dan terdengar lebih halus dan sopan dalam peringatan), **can** = boleh atau bisa.

rows.en: If we miss the deadline, the client will cancel the contract.
rows.id: Kalau kita melewatkan tenggat, klien akan membatalkan kontraknya.

rows.en: If you click on that link, you might get a virus.
rows.id: Kalau kamu klik tautan itu, bisa-bisa kena virus.

rows.en: If you finish the report by Thursday, you can leave early on Friday.
rows.id: Kalau laporannya selesai paling lambat Kamis, kamu boleh pulang cepat hari Jumat.

rows.en: As soon as I get approval from Pak Hasan, I'll let you know.
rows.id: Begitu dapat persetujuan dari Pak Hasan, saya kabari kamu.

rows.en: If you tell me about problems early, I won't be angry.
rows.id: Kalau kamu cerita soal masalah lebih awal, saya tidak akan marah.

blocks.text: **Softer warnings:** *If you don't fix it, the client **will** complain* sounds very sure, even a bit like a threat. *…the client **might** complain* is softer and more polite with colleagues and customers.

id.text: **Peringatan yang lebih halus:** *If you don't fix it, the client **will** complain* terdengar sangat yakin, bahkan agak seperti ancaman. *…the client **might** complain* lebih halus dan lebih sopan untuk rekan kerja dan pelanggan.

blocks.prompt: Your manager: 'If you finish the slides today, you ___ work from home tomorrow.'
blocks.explain: It's a deal: you're allowed, so use **can**: *you can work from home*. 'will can' is the Indonesian *akan bisa* trap (can never comes after will), and there's no *to* after might.

id.prompt: Manajermu: 'If you finish the slides today, you ___ work from home tomorrow.' Pilih yang benar.
id.explain: Ini kesepakatan: kamu boleh, jadi pakai **can**: *you can work from home*. 'will can' adalah jebakan *akan bisa* (can tidak pernah datang setelah will), dan tidak ada *to* setelah might.

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between in case and if?
Why can't I say 'Unless you don't hurry'?
Is as soon as the same as when?
Can I use will after unless or in case?

id.intro: Kamu sudah kenal first conditional: If it rains, I'll stay home. Hari ini kamu melangkah lebih jauh: lebih banyak jenis hasil (might, can, kalimat perintah), tiga kata yang berguna (unless, as soon as dan in case), dan cara memakainya untuk peringatan, kesepakatan dan janji di kantor. Pemanasan: apa yang akan kamu lakukan kalau hujan dalam perjalanan pulang hari ini?
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya in case dan if?
Kenapa tidak boleh bilang 'Unless you don't hurry'?
Apakah as soon as sama dengan when?
Boleh pakai will setelah unless atau in case?

assessment.fc-1: Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: If the server ___ (go) down again tonight, call me straight away.
assessment.fc-2: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: If the update will finish before 5, we can test the app today.
assessment.fc-3: Tulis ulang kalimat ini dengan unless. Artinya harus tetap sama: If you don't charge your laptop, it won't last until the end of the meeting.
assessment.fc-4: Lengkapi dengan in case atau if: Dimas has saved a copy of his presentation on a flash drive ___ the office laptop doesn't work.
assessment.fc-5: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: I'll message you as soon as the meeting will finish.
assessment.fc-6: Rekan kerjamu mau meluncurkan aplikasi baru besok tanpa mengujinya. Peringatkan dia. Lengkapi dengan bentuk negatif dari kata kerja dalam kurung: If we ___ (test) the app first, our customers will find the bugs.
assessment.fc-7: Baca pesan dari tim IT: 'Unless you change your password by Friday, your account will stop working on Monday.' Sari mengganti password-nya hari Kamis. Apakah akunnya masih bisa dipakai hari Senin? Jawab yes atau no.
